title: Woking
intro: A Surrey town surrounded by heath, canal and woodland, with Britain's first purpose-built mosque, H. G. Wells's Martians and one of the great gardens of England nearby.

items.name: Shah Jahan Mosque
items.blurb: Built in 1889, the first purpose-built mosque in Britain and Grade I listed.
items.tip: Visitors are welcome outside prayer times; dress modestly.

items.name: Horsell Common
items.blurb: Heathland, pine woods and sandpits on the edge of town, where H. G. Wells landed the Martians in The War of the Worlds.
items.tip: The peaceful Muslim Burial Ground garden is on the common's edge.

items.name: The Martian sculpture
items.blurb: A seven-metre steel tripod-fighting machine in the town centre, a tribute to H. G. Wells, who wrote The War of the Worlds while living in Woking.
items.tip: It stands in Crown Passage near the station.

items.name: Basingstoke Canal
items.blurb: A restored 18th-century canal running right through Woking, with a long towpath for walking and cycling and narrowboats in summer.
items.tip: Walk west towards St John's for the prettiest locks.

items.name: RHS Garden Wisley
items.blurb: The Royal Horticultural Society's flagship garden, with a great glasshouse, borders, woods and lakes, a short drive from Woking.
items.tip: Members get in free; go early on summer weekends.

items.name: Brookwood Cemetery
items.blurb: Opened in 1854 for London's dead, once served by its own railway from Waterloo; now a vast wooded cemetery with grand Victorian tombs.
items.tip: A quiet woodland walk as much as a cemetery.
